title: Experimentally mapped aggregation-critical protein regions, with circularity and prediction-concordance labels
description:
A hand-curated set of 17 protein regions across 8 proteins, shown experimentally to be required for, or to constitute the core of, protein aggregation. Every row was established by opening the source paper and checking the claim against it.

The dataset carries three columns that aggregation datasets usually lack, each because omitting it produces a benchmark that silently measures the wrong thing:

  • construct — which construct established the region. A region can be necessary in one construct and dispensable in another, and both results can be correct.
  • circularity_status — whether a predictor was in the discovery path. A region found by a predictor cannot be used to test that predictor. Circular rows are kept and labelled, not dropped.
  • stratum — whether experiment and prediction agree. Regions that are mapped cleanly tend to be the ones predictors find, so a dataset of well-mapped regions is enriched for agreement; only discordant rows can discriminate between predictors.

Limitations are stated in the data descriptor and should be read before use. The dataset is small and is not a random sample: the discordant stratum holds 4 documented rows, which supports a case series rather than a rate. 8 of 17 rows are not yet assessed for stratum. Rows are not independent. Most rows are recombinant or cell-based and cannot speak to aggregation in patients.
notes: Version 1.0.0, DOI 10.5281/zenodo.24290698 (version DOI; cite this one, not the concept DOI). Generated from data/regions.json by scripts/build_release.py and gated by scripts/validate_regions.py. See release/DATA_DESCRIPTOR.md.
